title: Security: $VAR/${VAR} variable expansion bypass in detectBashSubstitution and detectPowerShellSubstitution (GHSA-wpqr-6v78-jr5g)

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue provides a clear, actionable security bug report regarding variable expansion ($VAR/${VAR}) bypassing command substitution detection functions in packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.ts.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: The fix requires updating the command substitution detection logic in a single file (packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.ts) to handle variable expansion patterns ($VAR/${VAR}) and adding corresponding unit tests in packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.test.ts.

summary.problem: The shell command detection functions detectBashSubstitution and detectPowerShellSubstitution in packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.ts contain incomplete checks that allow variable expansion patterns ($VAR/${VAR}) to bypass security detection.
summary.root_cause: The detection logic in detectBashSubstitution and detectPowerShellSubstitution does not account for variable expansion syntaxes such as $VAR or ${VAR}, allowing command execution bypasses around security gates.
summary.context: This is a follow-up security issue related to GHSA-wpqr-6v78-jr5g, affecting both bash and PowerShell shell execution detection paths.

steps: Inspect detectBashSubstitution in packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.ts and enhance detection logic to handle $VAR and ${VAR} variable expansion patterns.
Inspect detectPowerShellSubstitution in packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.ts and enhance detection logic for variable expansions on PowerShell commands.
Implement safe variable allowlisting or comprehensive detection checks to ensure variable expansion bypasses are prevented.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: detectCommandSubstitution accurately identifies $VAR and ${VAR} variable expansion patterns in bash and PowerShell command strings and flags them appropriately.
verification_steps: Add unit test cases in packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.test.ts testing bash command inputs containing $VAR and ${VAR} expansions.
Add unit test cases testing PowerShell command inputs containing variable expansion patterns.
Run tests using Vitest to verify that all shell utility substitution tests pass.
